subject: humanities
passage: A printed geography of 1550 contains woodcut views of more than a hundred European towns, each labeled with the town's name, and historians have occasionally used these views to reconstruct the appearance of towns that were later rebuilt. Art historian Noor El-Amin compared the views closely. Several, she found, were printed from the very same wooden block: a view labeled as a town in Flanders shows the same walls, towers, and river, down to a small nick in the block's edge, as a view labeled as a town in Hungary hundreds of kilometers away. A few other views, by contrast, show distinctive buildings that still stand in the towns they name. El-Amin concludes that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: a view can be trusted only where something in it can be matched to the town it names.
choices.B: the views of the Flemish and Hungarian towns are accurate because both towns had similar walls and towers.
choices.C: none of the views in the geography depicts the actual appearance of the town it names.
choices.D: the printer visited each of the hundred towns in order to record its appearance.

explanation.why: The same block cannot show two towns hundreds of kilometers apart, so at least some views were not drawn from the towns they name. Yet a few views match buildings that still stand, so not every view is a stock image. The only safe rule is to trust a view when it can be checked against the town.
explanation.A: Correct. Some views are stock images reused for different towns, while a few can be tied to real buildings, so each view must be judged on its own evidence.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The views match down to a nick in the block because they were printed from one block, not because the towns resembled each other.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says a few views show distinctive buildings that still stand, so some views do depict their towns.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A block reused for towns in Flanders and Hungary shows that at least those views were not drawn from observation of each town.
